subject: EU authz cascade — entitlement validation and postmortem proposal
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@hearthpay.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@hearthpay.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike and auth failures — immediate impact summary

Hi Mateo,

We observed repeated 403/502 spikes across our EU checkout traffic between 09:54 and 10:09 UTC this morning. Our telemetry shows ~15 minutes where a subset of transactions failed authorization calls that hit Redwood. We lost ~1.8% of successful checkouts in that window.

Can you confirm whether this meets Redwood's availability SLO for eu-west regions and whether HearthPay is eligible for a credit? We rely on the 99.95% availability in the contract and this blip materially impacted a live promotion.

Attached are a small sampling of request ids and the client-side traces — we'll forward anything else you need. We need scope for an executive summary and an ETA for a postmortem so we can brief Ops and Finance.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Payments Ops
HearthPay

Attachments: request-ids-sample.csv (attachment), client-traces.zip (attachment)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@hearthpay.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Spike and auth failures — immediate impact summary

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the sample traces. I'm sorry for the disruption this morning. We're treating this as an availability event for the eu-west serving plane and have looped SRE and Support.

What we'll do next:
- I am requesting the raw server-side traces and auth service logs for 09:30–10:30 UTC (we'll pull KV cache & routing snapshots).
- Laura and David will validate whether the event meets the SLA windowing rules and confirm eligibility for a pro-rata credit or other remedy.
- We will schedule a postmortem (internal) and an external findings session with HearthPay — target: within 72 hours.

Can you confirm the list of impacted tenants (tenant ids) and your preferred 1-hour window(s) for a postmortem call? Also, we'll attach our raw log bundle here once ready.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: EU authz cascade — entitlement validation and postmortem proposal

Forwarding Elena's report and Mateo's ack. Quick summary for SRE/Entitlements:

- Event window: 2027-04-01 09:54:00–10:09:00 UTC (15 min) — customer reports auth failures spiking then.
- Impact: customer-supplied metric ~1.8% failed checkouts for the window.
- Region: eu-west (single region).
- Suspect vectors: routing failover + short-lived authz cache invalidation (based on early traces).

Per contract SLO (section 4.2), eligibility requires a verified region-level availability gap exceeding the per-month allowance. Given the short window, we need to check aggregated tenant impact across the month. If the event is classified as a Severity 2 regional availability blip, typical remedy is a pro-rata credit for the impacted window. If this is tied to throttling or misconfigured routing on the customer's side, that may change the calculation.

Actions I'm taking:
1) Pulling kernel-level serving traces and kv-cache dump (will attach: svc-trace-euw1-20270401.zip & authz-snapshot-20270401.json).
2) Requesting telemetry slice across all tenants in eu-west for Apr 1 to validate whether this was tenant-isolated or region-wide.
3) Drafting a proposed credit calculation once telemetry is verified (I estimate a conservative floor as 15 minutes out of the billing month for the affected tenant weight).

David — can you confirm whether fallback routing logs show any automatic fallbacks to lower-tier nodes that could have amplified the window?

Laura Bennett
Sr. Incident Manager | Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@hearthpay.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU authz cascade — entitlement validation and postmortem proposal

Elena / team,

Thanks for the samples — we completed the initial telemetry reconciliation. Findings in brief:
- Confirmed an authz cache invalidation cascade in eu-west starting 09:52 UTC with a peak error window 09:54–10:08 UTC.
- The event affected a set of tenants routed through a specific regional proxy cluster; HearthPay's traffic weight accounts for ~42% of the impacted capacity for that cluster during the window.
- Based on our contract language (SLO section 4.2.1: regional availability windows), HearthPay is eligible for a proportional credit for the verified window.

Proposed next steps:
1) Credit: offer a pro-rata credit calculated as (affected minutes / minutes in billing month) * monthly service fee. For transparency we'll provide the minute-level trace and the calculation worksheet.
2) Postmortem: I propose a customer-facing RCA call Monday 2027-04-04 at 14:00 UTC. If that works we'll send an invite and a postmortem draft beforehand.
3) Remediation: engineering will push a routing hardening patch and a KV-cache TTL tweak to reduce the risk of a cascade. We'll run the patch in canary tomorrow and share results.

I've attached the internal trace bundle and the quick calculation spreadsheet. Please confirm the Monday slot or propose an alternative.

Regards,
David Kim
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: svc-trace-euw1-20270401.zip, authz-snapshot-20270401.json, hearthpay-credit-calc.xlsx
